data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'tolere', meaning 'to endure, to bear, to suffer'. In Christian tradition, Tolentina is a name given to saints who demonstrated great patience and compassion in their lives. The name Tolentina carries the meaning “Tender, Merciful” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Tolentina usually hope their child will grow to embody tender, merciful and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Tolentina was the name of an ancient Roman city located near the Tyrrhenian Sea. It was an important port city in the Roman Republic and later the Roman Empire. Tolentina was also known as Talentum, a name derived from the Etruscan word for 'mound', referring to a sacred hill in the city.
historical_references.time_period: Roman Republic and Roman Empire (509 BC - 476 AD)

historical_references.reference: In the 4th century AD, Tolentina became an important Christian pilgrimage site due to the discovery of the relics of St. Pelagia, a legendary virgin martyr. Her tomb was located on the sacred hill of the city, and pilgrims from all over Europe came to pay their respects.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Christian name Tolentina is most commonly associated with the Italian city of Tolentino in the Marche region. In the religious context, it is the site of the Basilica of Saint Tolentino, which is dedicated to the saint of the same name. In the wine industry, Tolentina is a DOC wine produced in the area around the city. In the tourism industry, Tolentino is a popular destination for visitors to Italy, with attractions such as the Piazza Maggiore, the Palazzo Ducale, and the stunning natural beauty of the surrounding mountains. The name Tolentina is also used to refer to products associated with the city, such as olive oil and cheeses, which can be purchased online through various platforms such as Wine Searcher. On TripAdvisor, travelers can read reviews and plan their trip to Tolentino, while on Wikipedia, they can learn more about the history and culture of the city and its namesake saint.
